summary: B is the less invasive patch, but neither candidate satisfies the frozen contract and neither should merge unchanged.
reasons: Both expose Upload with ...UploadFileOption instead of the required exact ...FilesOption signature.
Both call Raw.Do directly and duplicate Add's request/response logic instead of routing the multipart body through FilesService.Add.
Both add prohibited association-option APIs and extend multipartbody rather than calling the established multipartbody.NewFile helper directly.

Both modify generic RawClient retry behavior despite the explicit instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery, and neither adds the required source-reader-error test coverage under Files.Upload tests specifically visible here (no such test is shown at all). However, helper-level behavior may exist; the visible omission is clear at Upload level and contract asks tests should cover it generally, so say neither adds required source-reader-error test coverage, period. Could helper existing tests cover? Patch not show, existing may. Contract asks tests should cover; only material maybe existing helper tests already source errors. Yet Upload propagation isn't tested. phrase no Upload test. Good. Need JSON. Candidate B retains existing WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions declarations unchanged, whereas A changes their public return types and introduces a multi-interface option hierarchy, creating additional API churn contrary to FilesOption stability requirements. Candidate B also avoids A's arbitrary WithFileFormField API and its broader multipart-field machinery, making B somewhat easier to remove or reshape into the contracted implementation.
risks_a: Changes public option-constructor return types from FilesOption to FilesRequestOption, which can break callers using those functions as typed values.
Adds numerous forbidden association APIs plus an unrestricted WithFileFormField escape hatch.

makeSeekableBodyReplayable changes Content-Length, closing, and retry semantics globally, including Files.Update; its claim that a failed Seek leaves the offset untouched is not guaranteed by io.Seeker contracts.
risks_b: Still has the wrong Upload signature and cannot accept existing FilesOption values.
Still duplicates Add logic, risking divergence in option handling and future error semantics.
Adds forbidden association options and a new WithUploadRequestOptions mechanism instead of preserving FilesOption behavior unchanged; also makes global Raw.Do replay changes outside task scope.
